ground_truth.title: Best Drip Coffee Makers (2026): Real Reviews, No Fluff
ground_truth.author: Kev
ground_truth.main_content:
Hey, I’m Kev, coffee nerd, home barista, and the guy behind the CoffeeKev YouTube channel. If you’ve been down the Google rabbit hole looking for the best drip coffee maker, you’ve probably run into a bunch of listicles that feel like someone just copied product descriptions from Amazon. This isn’t that.

I’ve personally tested every coffee maker on this list. I’m not paid by brands, I buy the gear myself, and if it’s not worth your time, I’ll tell you.

Drip coffee makers might not be the newest trend, but for millions of Americans, this is coffee. If that’s your vibe: hot, clean, classic filter coffee, you’re in the right place. Whether you’re after budget-friendly or boutique-level brewers, I’ve got real-world insight to help you pick the right machine.

Let’s dive in.

Technivorm Moccamaster KBT Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 40 ounces / 10 cups (more like 3-4 cups)
Model specialty: Thermal Carafe
Carafe: Stainless steel
Special features: Manual adjust drip speed
Brew time: 40 oz in 6 minutes
Material: Aluminum, stainless steel, plastic
SCA Certified?: Yes
Warranty: 5-year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

A True Icon of Drip Coffee

Technivorm has been crafting Moccamaster coffee makers in the Netherlands since the late 1960s. They haven’t changed much visually since, which is a big part of their appeal. The retro aesthetic and proven performance make Moccamaster a cult favorite among coffee lovers.

Why I Put This One First

If you asked me to name just two drip coffee makers I’d personally buy right now, the Moccamaster KBT would be one of them. The other? The Breville Precision Brewer, which I’ll cover next.

What Does “KBT” Mean?

The model name isn’t random.

“KB” refers to the rectangular body style.

“T” means it comes with a thermal carafe instead of a glass one with a hot plate.

That’s a huge plus if you want to keep your coffee hot without it sitting on a burner and tasting scorched after 30 minutes.

Manual Drip Speed Control

The KBT includes a simple flow control switch on the filter basket. You can:

Let it drip at full speed

Cut it to half speed

Or stop it altogether

This gives you some control over brew time (i.e., water contact time with the grounds), though it’s not as advanced as the programmable bloom and flow profiles you get with the Breville Precision Brewer.

Real Cup Capacity

The listed capacity is 10 cups (40 oz) —but let’s be real: 10 tiny cups.
If your idea of a normal cup of coffee is 10–12 oz (like most of us), you’re realistically getting about 3 to 4 cups per brew.
If you’re Snow White serving the seven dwarfs, maybe 10 four-ounce servings makes sense 😉

Why Moccamaster Delivers Such Good Coffee

There are two key reasons this machine has earned its legendary status:

1. The Showerhead Design

The Moccamaster’s unique metal showerhead gently and evenly disperses hot water over the coffee grounds. Unlike many other brewers, it covers a wider area for better saturation, contributing to consistent extraction and flavor.

2. Optimal & Stable Brew Temperature

Moccamaster nails the sweet spot for brewing temperature:

196°F to 205°F, which is exactly where you want it.

It also maintains temperature stability throughout the brew cycle, something many cheaper brewers can’t do.

If you’ve ever had bitter or uneven coffee from a bargain machine, it may have been due to unstable or overheated brewing. Moccamaster helps you avoid that.

Bonus: Pair It With the Moccamaster KM5 Grinder

If you’re thinking of going full Moccamaster, check out my video review of the KM5 burr grinder. It’s an excellent match for this machine.

Breville Precision Brewer Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 60 ounces
Carafe: Stainless steel
Special features: Far too many to fit here
Brew time: Various
Material: Mainly stainless steel
SCA Certified?: Yes
Warranty: 2-year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

One of My Two Top Picks

If you asked me to name just two drip brewers I’d recommend in 2025, this would be one of them (alongside the Technivorm Moccamaster). And that might sound surprising since the two machines couldn’t be more different.

But that’s exactly why they both make the list.

Moccamaster is a brilliant old-school brewer with classic simplicity.

Precision Brewer is the king of high-tech, new-age drip brewing.

Large Capacity Without the Gimmicks

This brewer can handle up to 60 oz of coffee, which is massive.
Breville keeps it honest by listing the volume in ounces instead of hyped-up “cup counts.”
That’s about 5–6 proper mugs of coffee (assuming a standard 10–12 oz cup), not tiny dollhouse cups.

SCA Certified Brewer

The Precision Brewer is SCA-certified, meaning it meets the Specialty Coffee Association’s strict standards for temperature stability, brew time, and extraction quality. That’s a solid endorsement for those serious about their coffee.

Advanced Brewing Technology

Here’s where it really stands out.

PID Temperature Control: Uses the same system as Breville’s espresso machines to maintain exact brew temps.

Adjustable Brew Temp: Dial in your preferred temperature.

Adjustable Bloom Time & Volume: Customize your pre-infusion phase.

Variable Flow Rate: Control how fast or slow the water flows through your coffee bed.

You can tweak every detail with the “My Brew” setting. Or, if you prefer to keep it simple, just hit “Gold Brew” to use pre-set SCA-approved settings. There’s also a “Fast” mode if you’re in a hurry.

Cold Brew, Auto Start & Pour-Over Compatible

Yep, it even does cold brew.

Plus, there’s an auto-start feature so you can wake up to fresh coffee, perfect if you don’t mind sacrificing a little freshness by pre-loading your grounds the night before.

Got a favorite pour-over setup like a V60 or Kalita Wave? Breville sells a pour-over adapter so you can use your own dripper in place of the standard basket.

Stainless Steel Thermal Carafe

The included double-walled thermal carafe keeps coffee hot for hours, especially when brewing full batches. No burnt taste from a hot plate, just proper thermal insulation.

Bottom Line: Control Meets Convenience

If you want advanced features, manual brewing control, and the flexibility to go hands-on or let the presets do the work, the Breville Precision Brewer is a top-tier choice.

From single cups to full carafes, from fast and easy to dialed-in pour-over precision, it can do it all. I’ve tested a lot of brewers, and this one truly stands out.

Cuisinart DCC-3200P1 Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 70 ounces / 14 cups (more like 6 or 7 cups)
Carafe: Glass
Special features: 24-hour programmability
Brew time: approx 12-15 minutes for a full pot
Material: Stainless steel and plastic
SCA Certified?: No
Warranty: 3-year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

A Budget-Friendly Pick That Delivers

After kicking things off with two high-end brewers, let’s bring things back down to earth with a solid, affordable option from a well-known name: Cuisinart.

The DCC-3200P1 may not be SCA certified like the Moccamaster or Breville Precision Brewer, but it’s a top seller for good reason: it brews a big pot of hot coffee reliably and at a great price.

Massive Brew Capacity

This brewer handles up to 70 oz of coffee. Yep, that’s a lot.
Officially, Cuisinart markets this as a 14-cup coffee maker … but take “cup counts” with a grain of salt. Unless you’re sipping 5-oz servings, it’s closer to 5–6 real cups (as in 10–12 oz mugs).

Fun fact: their more premium SCA-certified model (the CPO-850P1) holds just 64 oz but is labeled an 8-cup brewer. Go figure!

Not SCA Certified, But Still Impresses

No, it doesn’t have the Specialty Coffee Association stamp of approval—but that doesn’t mean it’s not worth a look. For everyday brewing at home, the DCC-3200P1 checks a lot of boxes, especially at this price point.

What Real Users Are Saying

With tens of thousands of Amazon reviews, this machine has a wealth of user feedback. Here are the most common takeaways:

✅ Brews Hot Coffee: One of the most consistently praised features is just how hot the coffee comes out—great news if you’ve ever been disappointed by lukewarm brews.

⚠️ Carafe Quirks: The small opening on the carafe makes it tricky to fill under the faucet. Yes, you can remove the plastic lid to make filling easier, but snapping it back into place is fiddly. Most users opt to fill it with the lid on, despite the tight space.

Bottom Line: Solid Value

If you’re looking for a big-capacity, no-frills coffee maker that brews piping hot coffee without breaking the bank, the Cuisinart DCC-3200P1 is a crowd favorite.

Ninja CE250 Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 60 ounces / 12 cups (more like 5 or 6 cups)
Carafe: Glass
Special features: Small batch brew & mid-brew auto pause
Brew time: Various
Material: Plastic and stainless steel
SCA Certified?: No
Warranty: 1-year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

A Budget Pick With Big Popularity

The Ninja CE250 is a low-cost drip coffee maker with enormous appeal and many Amazon reviews to prove it. It’s not one of Ninja’s SCA-certified machines (those are found in their “Specialty” line), but for everyday home brewing, this machine delivers solid performance at a wallet-friendly price.

60 oz Capacity (But Let’s Talk Real Cups)

Like most drip brewers, the CE250 claims a large cup count, 12 cups, or 60 oz, but that’s based on tiny 5-oz servings. Realistically, if you drink coffee like most of us do, you’re looking at about 5–6 standard-sized mugs (10–12 oz).

3 Brew Settings: Small Batch, Classic, and Rich

One standout feature is its brew flexibility:

Small Batch: Designed for 1–4 cups (translation: 1–2 normal mugs) without compromising strength.

Classic: For your everyday, smooth cup of drip coffee.

Rich: For a stronger, bolder brew without going overboard.

It’s a nice touch that makes this budget brewer feel like a more premium model.

Set It and Forget It: Delay Brew

Use the Delay Brew function to program your coffee the night before and wake up to a fresh pot. (No, it won’t bring it to your bedside… but we’re getting closer to that dream.)

Mid-Brew Pause + Removable Water Tank

The mid-brew pause means you can sneak a cup before the full pot is done without making a mess, great if you’re impatient (or just really need that first sip).
The removable water tank with a flip-top lid also makes filling super easy.

Hotter Brewing Tech (Yes, Really)

Ninja claims “Hotter Brewing Technology” thanks to an upgraded internal boiler. They’re a bit vague on the specifics, but in practice, it does seem to brew hotter coffee than many competitors in this price range, something that’s often a sore spot with cheaper machines.

Any Drawbacks?

There aren’t many red flags in user reviews, but one issue occasionally mentioned is rust developing on the warming plate over time. This is something to keep in mind with any hot plate-style machine.

Kev’s Tip: I’m not a fan of hot plates in general. Coffee left to sit and “cook” tends to develop off flavors. Instead, brew smaller batches using the Small Batch mode, or decant into a preheated thermal carafe or insulated travel mug to keep your coffee tasting great.

Check out my full Ninja Luxe Café Pro review here for a deeper dive into their latest innovation.

Krups Simply Brew Family Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 50.7 ounces / 10 cups (more like 4 or 5 cups)
Carafe: Glass
Special features: Pause & Serve
Brew time: Approx 5 minutes for a full pot
Material: Plastic and stainless steel
SCA Certified?: No
Warranty: 2 year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

Bare-Bones Brewing at a Bargain

The Krups Simply Brew Family is one of the most affordable drip coffee makers on the market, and it really shows. This machine is all about  simplicity. There are no fancy features, no digital display, no brew strength settings, just hot coffee made fast and cheap.

50 oz Capacity = “10 Cups”

Krups calls this a 10-cup machine, thanks to its 50-oz carafe. But as we’ve talked about in nearly every other review, nobody drinks 5-oz cups of coffee unless they’re in a dollhouse. In real-world terms, think about 4–5 standard 10–12 oz mugs per full brew.

Key Features: Pause & Serve + Auto Shutoff

Despite its low price, this Krups brewer does include a couple of essentials:

Pause & Serve: Lets you grab a cup mid-brew without making a mess.

1-Hour Keep Warm + Auto Shutoff: This device keeps your coffee warm for up to an hour before shutting off automatically, which is nice for safety and energy savings.

Build Quality: Basic, with Some Rough Edges

From the thousands of user reviews online, no major deal-breaking flaw pops up. That said, there are a few common annoyances reported, things like awkwardly shaped parts, cheap-feeling plastic, or minor design quirks that could’ve been smoothed out with just a little more attention.

But to be fair,  this  machine is super budget-friendly, and those little compromises come with the territory.

Heads-Up on the Different Versions

If you’re shopping on Amazon, you’ll notice that multiple Krups models are bundled under the same product listing. Be careful, these aren’t just color options. There are four versions listed, and they’re very different machines.

For example, the “Simply Brew to Go” version includes a thermal travel mug that looks like a different brewer. The price difference might be tempting, but ensure you select the one that matches your needs.

Kev’s Take

The Krups Simply Brew Family does the job if  you want a basic, budget-friendly drip coffee maker and you’re OK with skipping the bells and whistles. Just don’t expect premium materials or cutting-edge features at this price point.

Black & Decker 12-Cup Thermal Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 60 ounces / 12 cups (more like 4 or 5 cups)
Carafe: Insulated stainless steel
Special features: Evenstream Showerhead
Brew time: Approx 12-15 minutes for a full pot
Material: Plastic & stainless steel
SCA Certified?: No
Warranty: 2 year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

Wait, Black & Decker Makes Coffee Makers?

You might think of Black & Decker as the power tool brand, and you’d be right. But they’ve been in the home appliance game since 1984, when they acquired General Electric’s small household appliance division. So yeah, they’ve had time to figure out coffee.

Thermal Carafe at a Budget Price

Let’s start with what really stands out here: you’re getting a double-walled, vacuum-sealed thermal carafe, a feature usually reserved for higher-end brewers, at a very wallet-friendly price.

Most brewers in this price range ship with a standard glass carafe and a hot plate, which can lead to scorched coffee. So the inclusion of a thermal carafe here is a big win for flavor and freshness.

“EvenStream” Showerhead

Another feature you don’t usually see on budget brewers: an even saturation showerhead.

Now, I haven’t personally tested this brewer yet, so I can’t vouch for how well it actually performs, but I love that Black & Decker is thinking about extraction quality. Even water dispersion helps coffee grounds extract more evenly, which can drastically improve your cup.

This is the kind of detail I’d expect from more premium brewers, so again, great to see at this price point.

Brew Size: 12 Tiny Cups or 5–6 Real Ones

Like many manufacturers, Black & Decker lists this as a 12-cup brewer. But let’s be real: Those cups are  5-oz “micro cups.”  If you’re brewing real cups of coffee (10–12 oz), you’re looking at  around 5 to 6 servings, which is still solid given the  60-oz  brew capacity.

Kev’s Take

No, this isn’t going to compete head-to-head with top-tier SCA-certified brewers, but for a machine at this price, the  thermal carafe  and  attention to water dispersion  are genuinely impressive. If you’re after a  big-batch  drip brewer that keeps coffee hot without scorching it, this Black & Decker thermal brewer is well worth a look.

Mr. Coffee 12-Cup Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 60 ounces / 12 cups (more like 4 or 5 cups)
Carafe: Glass
Special features: Grab a brew, auto-pause
Brew time: 10-12 minutes for a full pot
Material: Plastic
SCA Certified?: No
Warranty: 1 year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

A Household Name in Coffee

You  can’t talk about drip coffee makers in the U.S. without mentioning Mr. Coffee. This isn’t some high-end, specialty-grade brewer. It’s not SCA-certified. You won’t find it in third-wave cafés. But for decades, Mr. Coffee has been one of the best-selling drip coffee brands in America, and there’s a good reason for that.

Budget-Friendly and Simple to Use

This is a very low-cost machine, and that’s clearly one reason it’s sold in such high volume. But price alone doesn’t explain the huge number of positive reviews it has collected.  People love this brewer because it does  exactly what it promises: it makes a pot of coffee without any fuss.

No fancy tech. No complicated controls. Just coffee. And for a lot of people, that’s exactly what they want.

Not for Specialty Coffee, and That’s Okay

This isn’t the machine for dialing in precise brew ratios, testing water temps, or brewing single-origin light roasts with a pour-over finesse. But it’s not trying to be.

If you’re a casual coffee drinker, someone who just wants a hot pot of coffee to get going in the morning without caring about “notes of bergamot and stone fruit”, then this is your kind of brewer.

“Grab-A-Cup” Auto Pause

One feature worth pointing out is Mr. Coffee’s “Grab-A-Cup” auto-pause, which is their version of the mid-brew pour feature. Like many other brewers, this lets you quickly sneak a cup while the machine is still brewing the full pot. Handy if you’re impatient (or half-asleep).

Kev’s Take

No, the Mr. Coffee 12-Cup isn’t a game-changer, but it doesn’t need to be. It’s cheap, reliable, easy to use, and it has a long track record of keeping everyday coffee drinkers happy.

If you’re just after a no-nonsense coffee maker that does its job without breaking the bank, Mr. Coffee continues to be a solid go-to.

Hamilton Beach 12-Cup And Single-Serve Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 96 ounces / 12 cups
Carafe: Glass
Special features: Separate single cup section
Brew time: 12-15 minutes for a full pot. 3-5 minutes for a single cup.
Material: Plastic & stainless steel
SCA Certified?: No
Warranty: 1 year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

Huge Brew Capacity

If you’re looking for volume, this brewer delivers. The Hamilton Beach 12-Cup & Single-Serve Coffee Maker boasts a massive  96-oz capacity, making it the  largest drip coffee maker on this list. Props to Hamilton Beach for sticking with the  8-oz  “real cup” standard instead of exaggerating the cup count like some other brands do. They could’ve called this a “24-cup” machine, but thankfully, they didn’t.

Dual Brewing Options: Carafe or Single Cup

What makes this brewer stand out is its dual brewing function. You can either brew a full pot or switch over to the dedicated single-serve side. Unlike some machines that include a pod brewer, this one gives you a true drip-style brew for individual servings.

A quick heads-up: some product images show a travel mug included, but it doesn’t come with one. That said, the single-serve side has an adjustable drip tray, and should fit most standard travel mugs easily.

Programmable Auto-Brew

The “Wake Up to Coffee” feature is a programmable timer that lets you schedule your brew ahead of time, whether it’s a full carafe or a single cup. That means you can have your travel mug filled and ready as soon as your alarm goes off.

Kev’s Take

This is a solid, versatile machine for households with varying coffee needs, maybe you brew a big pot on weekends and just want a quick cup on weekday mornings.

The only recurring complaint I came across while reading through a ton of reviews (OK, I skimmed…) was confusion around the travel mug. A lot of folks assumed it came included, and I can see how the product photos might lead you to think that. But to be fair, Hamilton Beach does clarify this in the fine print.

Bottom Line

If you’re after flexibility, big capacity, and solid everyday performance, and you don’t mind supplying your own travel mug, this Hamilton Beach brewer gives you a lot of bang for the buck.

Cuisinart 12-Cup And Single-Serve Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 40 ounces / 12 cups (more like 3 or 4 cups)
Carafe: Glass
Special features: Permanent Filter
Brew time: Various
Material: Plastic & stainless steel
SCA Certified?: No
Warranty: 3-year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

A Bestseller for a Reason

At the time of writing, this machine is one of the top-selling coffee makers on Amazon, so clearly, Cuisinart’s idea to combine single-serve brewing and a full drip system in one machine really hit the mark.

Questionable Cup Math

That said, Cuisinart might need a quick refresher on basic math. The carafe is labeled as 12 cups, but the water reservoir holds only 40 ounces. According to simple division, that would make each “cup” about 3.3 ounces. That’s about the size of a toddler’s sippy cup, not exactly what most people think of when they picture a satisfying cup of drip coffee.

Sure, a 3-ounce espresso makes sense, but drip coffee is all about sipping and savoring, and most people expect at least 8 to 12 ounces per cup.

Compatible With K-Cups & Reusable Pod

What sets this machine apart is that the single-serve side is compatible with Keurig K-Cups and other pod types. That means you can brew a full pot for the family, or just pop in a pod when you want a quick cup. Even better, it comes with a refillable pod, so you can use your own ground coffee instead of relying solely on pre-packaged pods.

24-Hour Programmable Start

You also get the 24-hour programmable brew timer, which is fairly standard at this price point but definitely welcome. It lets you set up your brew the night before so you can wake up to fresh coffee, whether you’re brewing a full pot or just a single cup.

Kev’s Take

This is a versatile machine, ideal for homes where one person wants a big carafe and another just needs a single cup to go. While the “12-cup” label is definitely a stretch, the convenience of having both drip and pod brewing in one tidy unit is hard to beat.

Bonavita 8-Cup Coffee Maker with Thermal Carafe BV1500TS 

Features

Max Brew: 1.3l / 8 cups
Carafe: Thermal, stainless steel.
Special features: Wide showerhead design, preinfusion
Brew time: Around 6 minutes
Material: Stainless steel & plastic
SCA Certified?: Yes
Warranty: 2-year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

A Brand That’s Still Brewing

Bonavita has faced its fair share of recent controversy, from legal disputes between its manufacturer and distributor to rumors that the brand was on its way out. But like Mark Twain once said, reports of its death have been greatly exaggerated. According to the latest updates, those issues seem to be resolved, and Bonavita is back in action, alive and brewing.

Designed for Small Batch Excellence

While its larger sibling holds SCA certification, this smaller-capacity brewer shares many of the same high-quality design features. It brews between 195–205°F, which is exactly the temperature range you want for optimal coffee extraction. The showerhead design ensures even saturation, especially for smaller batches, and there’s even an optional pre-infusion mode, a feature often reserved for higher-end brewers.

Reliable, but Reputation Took a Hit

This machine has sold well and is generally well-loved on Amazon, but its overall rating isn’t quite what you’d expect for such a well-respected brewer. Much of the recent negativity seems tied to the fallout from Bonavita’s distributor issues.

To clarify:

If you purchased a Bonavita machine before January 1, 2021, your warranty is technically under the old distributor, who no longer offers support.

Bonavita says they’ll still offer customer support, but no replacements or refunds for those older units.
This situation has understandably ruffled feathers across Amazon reviews, Reddit threads, and coffee forums.

Minor Flaws, Nothing Major

As for the product itself, most complaints are relatively minor.

The thermal carafe can be tough to fully empty, especially that last bit of coffee.

Pouring without the lid can be a little messy, which might be frustrating if you’re in a hurry.

Kev’s Take

If you’re looking for a compact, no-nonsense drip brewer that still ticks most of the specialty boxes, including proper brewing temp, a pre-infusion option, and a thermal carafe, this Bonavita is a solid option. Just be sure your unit was purchased recently to avoid warranty issues.

Oxo 8-Cup Drip Coffee Maker

Features

Max Brew: 64 ounces / 8 cups
Carafe: Thermal, dual-walled stainless steel.
Special features: Single serve option. Rainmaker shower head
Brew time: Approx 6-8 minutes for a full pot
Material: Stainless steel & plastic
SCA Certified?: Yes
Warranty: 2-year manufacturer’s warranty

Kev’s Observations

Certified for Specialty Brewing

The OXO 8-Cup Coffee Maker is another SCA-certified brewer, which already gives it a leg up in terms of quality assurance. One thing I’ve noticed across these certified brewers is that they tend to stick to the realistic 8-ounce “standard cup” size —no wild marketing claims like “12 cups” when they mean 4-ounce espresso shots.

Smart Features for Better Brewing

On paper, this is a well-equipped machine. Key features include:

The Rainmaker™ showerhead, which evenly disperses hot water over the grounds

BetterBrew™ Precision, a system that optimizes brew temp, time, and volume

A double-walled, vacuum-insulated thermal carafe

A single-serve brew mode, which is handy for quick solo cups

All of this at a price point makes it one of the best-value SCA-certified drip brewers on the market.

Excellent Water Distribution

I have to say, the Rainmaker showerhead does look impressive. One of my only gripes with the Breville Precision Brewer was its showerhead’s size and distribution radius, it concentrated water too much toward the center.
With the OXO Rainmaker, though, you can expect a much more even spread of water over the coffee bed, which improves saturation and helps avoid uneven extraction.

Single-Cup Convenience, or Brew a Whole Pot

OXO gives you the option to brew a single cup or a full 8-cup carafe, which is great if you’re switching between solo sips and serving guests. That said,  customer reviews  have mixed feelings  about the carafe’s heat retention.

And I get it. I’ve seen this with other brewers, too. If you’re only brewing a small amount and the  carafe is cold, it’ll zap the heat from your coffee as it brews, and the final temperature will not be  there by the time the pot is done.

Pre-warming the carafe is highly recommended if you’re brewing less than a full pot. The same goes for the mug if you’re using single-serve mode. A stone-cold cup will soak up the first ounces of heat like a sponge.

Kev’s Take

The OXO 8-Cup is a great compact brewer for people who want true drip coffee without going overboard on features or price. It’s especially ideal if you want SCA-certified quality in a simple package, and it’s great for both everyday sippers and weekend entertainers.

Drip Coffee Makers FAQs

Q: Is there a difference between drip coffee makers?

A: Yes, for sure. The biggest difference is that there are cheap, domestic drip coffee makers, and there are specialty drip coffee makers. The best way to ensure you’re getting the latter if this is what you want is to look for an SCA-approved drip coffee maker, as a number of the options above are. The biggest difference between “standard” drip coffee makers and specialty brewers is that brewers made for specialty coffee are designed to deliver a specific, precise brew temperature, and other key elements include the design of the showerhead to ensure evenly saturated grinds, specific flow rate, and bloom time & volume.

Q: Is French press coffee better than drip?

A: Better is a subjective word, there’s really no such concept as “better”, just “better for me” – so where French Press vs drip coffee is concerned, which is better just comes down to which you prefer. French press coffee is characteristically a heavier brew in terms of mouthfeel, and usually a more intense brew in terms of flavor, although you can adjust this with your brewing technique.

Q: How do you make drip coffee taste better?

A: The number one way to make your coffee taste better, regardless of the brew method, is to use better quality coffee. Look for coffee from a specialty small-batch coffee roaster, which has a roasted-on date of between 2-4 weeks from when you purchase it, and try various different coffees, as there are so many different tasting coffees available, from different origins, from different subspecies of Arabica.

Want to improve your coffee? Then watch this helpful guide

Q: Is Espresso better than drip coffee?

A: If you prefer espresso to drip coffee, then yes. If you prefer drip coffee to espresso, then no. There’s no such thing as better or worse where taste is concerned, as we all have different taste buds. In fact, for me, it would depend on when you ask me. There are times when I’m in the mood for espresso or espresso-based drinks, and there are times when I’m in the mood for drip coffee.

Q: Do all drip coffee makers taste the same?

A: I’ve never actually tasted a drip coffee maker, so I can’t help you with this one;-). If you’re referring to the taste of the drip coffee from various drip coffee makers, then no. Generally speaking, if you’re buying a low-priced “normal” drip coffee maker, then if you were to line up a number of them and try them all with the same coffee, I think you’d probably find that they’re all quite similar when it comes to taste.

If you were to brew a pot of the same coffee with a lower-cost “normal” drip coffee maker and also brew the same coffee with one of the premium, more home barista-grade specialty drip coffee brewers, then I would expect most people to be able to notice a difference in the taste. Not only this, but I’d expect the specialty coffee brewer to be more consistent from one pot to the next.

A: Do you have milk with drip coffee?

A: WHAT???? Hehe, I’m just kidding. Sure, if you like milk, creamer, half & half, whatever you like with your drip coffee, why not? Heck, some people are even putting butter in their coffee these days! I say each to their own, personally, I drink my filter coffee (which is another label for drip coffee, by the way) black.

It does depend on what coffee you’re using, though. Many people add stuff to coffee, such as milk, creamer, and/or sugar or syrups, because it’s bitter and needs sweetening, and this is largely to do with the coffee itself.

If you’re using store-bought “commodity” coffee (coffee that is traded as a commodity like sugar and grain), it’s usually roasted dark to remove taste defects. It’s inherently bitter, which some people like, but some people don’t, hence the addition of stuff to sweeten it and mask the bitterness.

The first change you’ll probably notice if you start drinking specialty coffee is that you’re no longer as inclined to put anything in your coffee other than your face.

Q: Is Nespresso drip coffee?

A: In a word, no. The original Nespresso machines make an espresso-style drink, short concentrated shots, which aren’t technically espresso as it’s brewed differently, but it’s closest to espresso. You can, of course, add hot water to Nespresso, and if you do that, then you’ll make something which is more akin to an Americano than drip coffee, which is similar but not quite the same. Generally speaking, drip coffee is lighter and cleaner than Americano and the Americano style coffee you’d get from adding hot water to a Nespresso.

There’s also the newer Nespresso Vertuo machine, and this does have the option of pour-over style pods, but to me, these don’t look or taste anything like drip coffee. They have a big foamy crema, which is something I’d associate more with Americano, and they have the body and flavor of Americano more than drip coffee, just my humble opinion from the Nespresso Vertuo pods I’ve tried.

ground_truth.main_content_markdown:
Hey, I’m Kev, coffee nerd, home barista, and the guy behind the [CoffeeKev YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@Coffee_Kev). If you’ve been down the Google rabbit hole looking for the best drip coffee maker, you’ve probably run into a bunch of listicles that feel like someone just copied product descriptions from Amazon. This isn’t that.

I’ve personally tested every coffee maker on this list. I’m not paid by brands, I buy the gear myself, and if it’s not worth your time, I’ll tell you.

Drip coffee makers might not be the newest trend, but for millions of Americans, this *is* coffee. If that’s your vibe: hot, clean, classic filter coffee, you’re in the right place. Whether you’re after budget-friendly or boutique-level brewers, I’ve got real-world insight to help you pick the right machine.

Let’s dive in.

### Technivorm Moccamaster KBT Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 40 ounces / 10 cups (more like 3-4 cups)
**Model specialty:** Thermal Carafe
**Carafe:** Stainless steel
**Special features:** Manual adjust drip speed
**Brew time:** 40 oz in 6 minutes
**Material:** Aluminum, stainless steel, plastic
**SCA Certified?:** Yes
**Warranty:** 5-year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### A True Icon of Drip Coffee

Technivorm has been crafting Moccamaster coffee makers in the Netherlands since the late 1960s. They haven’t changed much visually since, which is a big part of their appeal. The retro aesthetic and proven performance make Moccamaster a cult favorite among coffee lovers.

#### Why I Put This One First

If you asked me to name just two drip coffee makers I’d personally buy right now, the Moccamaster KBT would be one of them. The other? [The Breville Precision Brewer](https://coffeekev.com/breville-precision-brewer-coffee-maker-review/), which I’ll cover next.

#### What Does “KBT” Mean?

The model name isn’t random.

**“KB”** refers to the rectangular body style.

**“T”** means it comes with a **thermal carafe** instead of a glass one with a hot plate.

That’s a huge plus if you want to keep your coffee hot without it sitting on a burner and tasting scorched after 30 minutes.

#### Manual Drip Speed Control

The KBT includes a simple flow control switch on the filter basket. You can:

Let it drip at full speed

Cut it to half speed

Or stop it altogether

This gives you some control over brew time (i.e., water contact time with the grounds), though it’s not as advanced as the programmable bloom and flow profiles you get with the Breville Precision Brewer.

#### Real Cup Capacity

The listed capacity is **10 cups (40 oz)** -but let’s be real: 10 *tiny* cups.
If your idea of a normal cup of coffee is 10-12 oz (like most of us), you’re realistically getting about 3 to 4 cups per brew.
If you’re Snow White serving the seven dwarfs, maybe 10 four-ounce servings makes sense 😉

#### Why Moccamaster Delivers Such Good Coffee

There are two key reasons **this** machine has earned its legendary status:

##### 1. The Showerhead Design

The Moccamaster’s unique metal showerhead gently and evenly disperses hot water over the coffee grounds. Unlike many other brewers, it covers a wider area for better saturation, contributing to consistent extraction and flavor.

##### 2. Optimal & Stable Brew Temperature

Moccamaster nails the sweet spot for brewing temperature:

**196°F to 205°F**, which is exactly where you want it.

It also maintains **temperature stability** throughout the brew cycle, something many cheaper brewers can’t do.

If you’ve ever had bitter or uneven coffee from a bargain machine, it may have been due to unstable or overheated brewing. Moccamaster helps you avoid that.

### Bonus: Pair It With the Moccamaster KM5 Grinder

If you’re thinking of going full Moccamaster, check out my video review of the KM5 [burr grinder](https://coffeekev.com/best-coffee-grinders/). It’s an excellent match for this machine.

### Breville Precision Brewer Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 60 ounces
**Carafe:** Stainless steel
**Special features:** Far too many to fit here
**Brew time:** Various
**Material:** Mainly stainless steel
**SCA Certified?:** Yes
**Warranty:** 2-year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### One of My Two Top Picks

If you asked me to name just two drip brewers I’d recommend in 2025, this would be one of them (alongside the Technivorm Moccamaster). And that might sound surprising since the two machines couldn’t be more different.

But that’s exactly why they both make the list.

**Moccamaster** is a brilliant *old-school* brewer with classic simplicity.

**Precision Brewer** is the king of *high-tech, new-age* drip brewing.

#### Large Capacity Without the Gimmicks

This brewer can handle up to **60 oz** of coffee, which is massive.
Breville keeps it honest by listing the volume in ounces instead of hyped-up “cup counts.”
That’s about **5-6 proper mugs** of coffee (assuming a standard 10-12 oz cup), not tiny dollhouse cups.

#### SCA Certified Brewer

The Precision Brewer is [**SCA-certified**](https://sca.coffee/certified-home-brewer), meaning it meets the **Specialty Coffee Association’s strict standards** for temperature stability, brew time, and extraction quality. That’s a solid endorsement for those serious about their coffee.

#### Advanced Brewing Technology

Here’s where it really stands out.

**PID Temperature Control**: Uses the same system as [Breville’s espresso machines](https://coffeekev.com/best-breville-espresso-machine/) to maintain exact brew temps.

**Adjustable Brew Temp**: Dial in your preferred temperature.

**Adjustable Bloom Time & Volume**: Customize your pre-infusion phase.

**Variable Flow Rate**: Control how fast or slow the water flows through your coffee bed.

You can tweak every detail with the **“My Brew”** setting. Or, if you prefer to keep it simple, just hit **“Gold Brew”** to use pre-set SCA-approved settings. There’s also a **“Fast”** mode if you’re in a hurry.

#### Cold Brew, Auto Start & Pour-Over Compatible

Yep, it even does **cold brew**.

Plus, there’s an **auto-start** feature so you can **wake up to fresh coffee**, perfect if you don’t mind sacrificing a little freshness by pre-loading your grounds the night before.

Got a favorite pour-over setup like a V60 or Kalita Wave? Breville sells a **pour-over adapter** so you can use your own dripper in place of the standard basket.

#### Stainless Steel Thermal Carafe

The included **double-walled thermal carafe** keeps coffee hot for hours, especially when brewing full batches. No burnt taste from a hot plate, just proper thermal insulation.

#### Bottom Line: Control Meets Convenience

If you want **advanced features**, **manual brewing control**, and the **flexibility** to go hands-on or let the presets do the work, the Breville Precision Brewer is a top-tier choice.

From single cups to full carafes, from fast and easy to dialed-in pour-over precision, it can do it all. I’ve tested a lot of brewers, and this one truly stands out.

### Cuisinart DCC-3200P1 Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 70 ounces / 14 cups (more like 6 or 7 cups)
**Carafe:** Glass
**Special features:** 24-hour programmability
**Brew time:** approx 12-15 minutes for a full pot
**Material:** Stainless steel and plastic
**SCA Certified?:** No
**Warranty:** 3-year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### A Budget-Friendly Pick That Delivers

After kicking things off with two high-end brewers, let’s bring things back down to earth with a solid, affordable option from a well-known name: **Cuisinart**.

The **DCC-3200P1** may not be SCA certified like the Moccamaster or Breville Precision Brewer, but it’s a top seller for good reason: it brews a big pot of hot coffee reliably and at a great price.

#### Massive Brew Capacity

This brewer handles up to **70 oz** of coffee. Yep, that’s a lot.
Officially, Cuisinart markets this as a **14-cup coffee maker** ... but take “cup counts” with a grain of salt. Unless you’re sipping 5-oz servings, it’s closer to **5-6 real cups** (as in 10-12 oz mugs).

Fun fact: their more premium SCA-certified model (the CPO-850P1) holds just 64 oz but is labeled an 8-cup brewer. Go figure!

#### Not SCA Certified, But Still Impresses

No, it doesn’t have the Specialty Coffee Association stamp of approval-but that doesn’t mean it’s not worth a look. For everyday brewing at home, the DCC-3200P1 checks a lot of boxes, especially at this price point.

#### What Real Users Are Saying

With tens of thousands of Amazon reviews, this machine has a wealth of user feedback. Here are the most common takeaways:

✅ **Brews Hot Coffee**: One of the most consistently praised features is just how hot the coffee comes out-great news if you’ve ever been disappointed by lukewarm brews.

⚠️ **Carafe Quirks**: The **small opening on the carafe** makes it tricky to fill under the faucet. Yes, you can remove the plastic lid to make filling easier, but snapping it back into place is fiddly. Most users opt to fill it with the lid on, despite the tight space.

#### Bottom Line: Solid Value

If you’re looking for a **big-capacity, no-frills coffee maker** that brews **piping hot coffee** without breaking the bank, the **Cuisinart DCC-3200P1** is a crowd favorite.

### Ninja CE250 Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 60 ounces / 12 cups (more like 5 or 6 cups)
**Carafe:** Glass
**Special features:** Small batch brew & mid-brew auto pause
**Brew time:** Various
**Material:** Plastic and stainless steel
**SCA Certified?:** No
**Warranty:** 1-year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### A Budget Pick With Big Popularity

The **Ninja CE250** is a **low-cost drip coffee maker** with enormous appeal and many Amazon reviews to prove it. It’s not one of Ninja’s SCA-certified machines (those are found in their “Specialty” line), but for everyday home brewing, this machine delivers solid performance at a wallet-friendly price.

#### 60 oz Capacity (But Let’s Talk Real Cups)

Like most drip brewers, the CE250 claims a large cup count, **12 cups, or 60 oz,** but that’s based on tiny 5-oz servings. Realistically, if you drink coffee like most of us do, you’re looking at **about 5-6 standard-sized mugs** (10-12 oz).

#### 3 Brew Settings: Small Batch, Classic, and Rich

One standout feature is its **brew flexibility**:

**Small Batch**: Designed for 1-4 cups (translation: 1-2 normal mugs) without compromising strength.

**Classic**: For your everyday, smooth cup of drip coffee.

**Rich**: For a stronger, bolder brew without going overboard.

It’s a nice touch that makes this budget brewer feel like a more premium model.

#### Set It and Forget It: Delay Brew

Use the **Delay Brew** function to program your coffee the night before and wake up to a fresh pot. (No, it won’t bring it to your bedside... but we’re getting closer to that dream.)

#### Mid-Brew Pause + Removable Water Tank

The **mid-brew pause** means you can sneak a cup before the full pot is done without making a mess, great if you’re impatient (or just really need that first sip).
The **removable water tank** with a flip-top lid also makes filling super easy.

#### Hotter Brewing Tech (Yes, Really)

Ninja claims “Hotter Brewing Technology” thanks to an upgraded internal boiler. They’re a bit vague on the specifics, but in practice, it does seem to **brew hotter coffee** than many competitors in this price range, something that’s often a sore spot with cheaper machines.

#### Any Drawbacks?

There aren’t many red flags in user reviews, but one issue occasionally mentioned is **rust developing on the warming plate** over time. This is something to keep in mind with any hot plate-style machine.

**Kev’s Tip:** I’m not a fan of hot plates in general. Coffee left to sit and “cook” tends to develop off flavors. Instead, brew smaller batches using the Small Batch mode, or decant into a preheated thermal carafe or insulated travel mug to keep your coffee tasting great.

Check out my full [Ninja Luxe Café Pro review here](https://coffeekev.com/ninja-luxe-cafe-701-pro-review/) for a deeper dive into their latest innovation.

### Krups Simply Brew Family Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 50.7 ounces / 10 cups (more like 4 or 5 cups)
**Carafe:** Glass
**Special features:** Pause & Serve
**Brew time:** Approx 5 minutes for a full pot
**Material:** Plastic and stainless steel
**SCA Certified?:** No
**Warranty:** 2 year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### Bare-Bones Brewing at a Bargain

The **Krups Simply Brew Family** is one of the most affordable drip coffee makers on the market, and it really shows. This machine is all about  **simplicity**. There are no fancy features, no digital display, no brew strength settings, just hot coffee made fast and cheap.

#### 50 oz Capacity = ”10 Cups“

Krups calls this a **10-cup machine**, thanks to its 50-oz carafe. But as we’ve talked about in nearly every other review, **nobody drinks 5-oz cups** of coffee unless they’re in a dollhouse. In real-world terms, think **about 4-5 standard 10-12 oz mugs** per full brew.

#### Key Features: Pause & Serve + Auto Shutoff

Despite its low price, this Krups brewer does include a couple of essentials:

**Pause & Serve**: Lets you grab a cup mid-brew without making a mess.

**1-Hour Keep Warm + Auto Shutoff**: This device keeps your coffee warm for up to an hour before shutting off automatically, which is nice for safety and energy savings.

#### Build Quality: Basic, with Some Rough Edges

From the thousands of user reviews online, no major deal-breaking flaw pops up. That said, there are **a few common annoyances** reported, things like awkwardly shaped parts, cheap-feeling plastic, or minor design quirks that could’ve been smoothed out with just a little more attention.

But to be fair,  this  machine is super budget-friendly, and those little compromises come with the territory.

#### Heads-Up on the Different Versions

If you’re shopping on Amazon, you’ll notice that **multiple Krups models** are bundled under the same product listing. Be careful, these aren’t just color options. There are four versions listed, and they’re **very different machines**.

For example, the **”Simply Brew to Go“** version includes a **thermal travel mug** that looks like a different brewer. The price difference might be tempting, but ensure you select the one that matches your needs.

#### Kev’s Take

The Krups Simply Brew Family does the job if  **you want a basic, budget-friendly drip coffee maker** and you’re OK with skipping the bells and whistles. Just don’t expect premium materials or cutting-edge features at this price point.

### Black & Decker 12-Cup Thermal Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 60 ounces / 12 cups (more like 4 or 5 cups)
**Carafe:** Insulated stainless steel
**Special features:** Evenstream Showerhead
**Brew time:** Approx 12-15 minutes for a full pot
**Material:** Plastic & stainless steel
**SCA Certified?:** No
**Warranty:** 2 year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### Wait, Black & Decker Makes Coffee Makers?

You might think of **Black & Decker** as the power tool brand, and you’d be right. But they’ve been in the home appliance game since **1984**, when they acquired General Electric’s small household appliance division. So yeah, they’ve had time to figure out coffee.

#### Thermal Carafe at a Budget Price

Let’s start with what **really stands out** here: you’re getting a **double-walled, vacuum-sealed thermal carafe,** a feature usually reserved for higher-end brewers, at a **very wallet-friendly price**.

Most brewers in this price range ship with a standard glass carafe and a hot plate, which can lead to scorched coffee. So the inclusion of a thermal carafe here is a **big win for flavor and freshness**.

#### ”EvenStream“ Showerhead

Another feature you don’t usually see on budget brewers: an **even saturation showerhead**.

Now, I haven’t personally tested this brewer yet, so I can’t vouch for how well it actually performs, but I love that **Black & Decker is thinking about extraction quality**. Even water dispersion helps coffee grounds extract more evenly, which can drastically improve your cup.

This is the kind of detail I’d expect from more premium brewers, so again, **great to see at this price point**.

#### Brew Size: 12 Tiny Cups or 5-6 Real Ones

Like many manufacturers, Black & Decker lists this as a **12-cup brewer**. But let’s be real: Those cups are  **5-oz ”micro cups.“**  If you’re brewing real cups of coffee (10-12 oz), you’re looking at  **around 5 to 6 servings**, which is still solid given the  **60-oz**  brew capacity.

#### Kev’s Take

No, this isn’t going to compete head-to-head with top-tier **SCA-certified brewer**s, but for a machine at this price, the  **thermal carafe**  and  **attention to water dispersion**  are genuinely impressive. If you’re after a  **big-batch**  drip brewer that keeps coffee hot without scorching it, this **Black & Decker thermal brewer is well worth a look**.

### Mr. Coffee 12-Cup Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 60 ounces / 12 cups (more like 4 or 5 cups)
**Carafe:** Glass
**Special features:** Grab a brew, auto-pause
**Brew time:** 10-12 minutes for a full pot
**Material:** Plastic
**SCA Certified?:** No
**Warranty:** 1 year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### A Household Name in Coffee

**You**  can’t talk about drip coffee makers in the U.S. without mentioning Mr. Coffee. This isn’t some high-end, specialty-grade brewer. It’s not [SCA-certified](https://sca.coffee/certified-home-brewer). You won’t find it in third-wave cafés. But for decades, Mr. Coffee has been **one of the best-selling drip coffee brands in America**, and there’s a good reason for that.

#### Budget-Friendly and Simple to Use

This is a **very low-cost machine**, and that’s clearly one reason it’s sold in such high volume. But price alone doesn’t explain the **huge number of positive reviews** it has collected.  People love this brewer because it does  **exactly what it promises:** it makes a pot of coffee without any fuss.

No fancy tech. No complicated controls. Just coffee. And for a lot of people, **that’s exactly what they want**.

#### Not for Specialty Coffee, and That’s Okay

This isn’t the machine for dialing in precise brew ratios, testing water temps, or brewing single-origin light roasts with a pour-over finesse. **But it’s not trying to be**.

If you’re a casual coffee drinker, someone who just wants a hot pot of coffee to get going in the morning without caring about ”notes of bergamot and stone fruit“, then this is your kind of brewer.

#### ”Grab-A-Cup“ Auto Pause

One feature worth pointing out is **Mr. Coffee’s ”Grab-A-Cup“ auto-pause**, which is their version of the mid-brew pour feature. Like many other brewers, this lets you quickly sneak a cup while the machine is still brewing the full pot. Handy if you’re impatient (or half-asleep).

#### Kev’s Take

No, the **Mr. Coffee 12-Cup** isn’t a game-changer, but it **doesn’t need to be**. It’s **cheap, reliable, easy to use**, and it has a long track record of keeping everyday coffee drinkers happy.

If you’re just after a **no-nonsense coffee maker that does its job** without breaking the bank, **Mr. Coffee continues to be a solid go-to**.

### Hamilton Beach 12-Cup And Single-Serve Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 96 ounces / 12 cups
**Carafe:** Glass
**Special features:** Separate single cup section
**Brew time:** 12-15 minutes for a full pot. 3-5 minutes for a single cup.
**Material:** Plastic & stainless steel
**SCA Certified?:** No
**Warranty:** 1 year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### Huge Brew Capacity

If you’re looking for volume, this brewer delivers. The Hamilton Beach 12-Cup & [Single-Serve Coffee Maker](https://coffeekev.com/best-single-serve-coffee-maker/) boasts a massive  **96-oz capacity**, making it the  **largest drip coffee maker on this list**. Props to Hamilton Beach for sticking with the  **8-oz**  ”real cup“ standard instead of exaggerating the cup count like some other brands do. They could’ve called this a ”24-cup“ machine, but thankfully, they didn’t.

#### Dual Brewing Options: Carafe or Single Cup

What makes this brewer stand out is its **dual brewing function**. You can either brew a full pot or switch over to the **dedicated single-serve side**. Unlike some machines that include a pod brewer, this one gives you a **true drip-style brew** for individual servings.

A quick heads-up: some product images show a travel mug included, but **it doesn’t come with one**. That said, the single-serve side has an **adjustable drip tray**, and should fit most standard travel mugs easily.

#### Programmable Auto-Brew

The **”Wake Up to Coffee“ feature** is a programmable timer that lets you schedule your brew ahead of time, whether it’s a full carafe or a single cup. That means you can have your travel mug filled and ready **as soon as your alarm goes off**.

#### Kev’s Take

This is a **solid, versatile machine** for households with varying coffee needs, maybe you brew a big pot on weekends and just want a quick cup on weekday mornings.

The only recurring complaint I came across while reading through a ton of reviews (OK, I skimmed...) was confusion around the travel mug. A lot of folks assumed it came included, and I can see how the product photos might lead you to think that. But to be fair, **Hamilton Beach does clarify this in the fine print**.

#### Bottom Line

If you’re after **flexibility, big capacity, and solid everyday performance,** and you don’t mind supplying your own travel mug, this Hamilton Beach brewer gives you **a lot of bang for the buck**.

### Cuisinart 12-Cup And Single-Serve Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 40 ounces / 12 cups (more like 3 or 4 cups)
**Carafe:** Glass
**Special features:** Permanent Filter
**Brew time:** Various
**Material:** Plastic & stainless steel
**SCA Certified?:** No
**Warranty:** 3-year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### A Bestseller for a Reason

At the time of writing, this machine is **one of the top-selling coffee makers on Amazon**, so clearly, **Cuisinart’s idea to combine single-serve brewing and a full drip system** in one machine really hit the mark.

#### Questionable Cup Math

That said, Cuisinart might need a quick refresher on basic math. The carafe is labeled as **12 cups**, but the water reservoir holds **only 40 ounces**. According to simple division, that would make each ”cup“ about **3.3 ounces**. That’s about the size of a toddler’s sippy cup, not exactly what most people think of when they picture a satisfying cup of drip coffee.

Sure, a 3-ounce espresso makes sense, but **drip coffee is all about sipping and savoring**, and most people expect at least 8 to 12 ounces per cup.

#### Compatible With K-Cups & Reusable Pod

What sets this machine apart is that the **single-serve side is compatible with Keurig K-Cups** and other pod types. That means you can brew a full pot for the family, or just pop in a pod when you want a quick cup. Even better, it comes with a **refillable pod**, so you can use your own ground coffee instead of relying solely on pre-packaged pods.

#### 24-Hour Programmable Start

You also get the **24-hour programmable brew timer**, which is fairly standard at this price point but definitely welcome. It lets you set up your brew the night before so you can wake up to fresh coffee, whether you’re brewing a full pot or just a single cup.

#### Kev’s Take

This is a versatile machine, ideal for homes where one person wants a big carafe and another just needs a single cup to go. While the **”12-cup“ label is definitely a stretch**, the convenience of having **both drip and pod brewing** in one tidy unit is hard to beat.

### Bonavita 8-Cup Coffee Maker with Thermal Carafe BV1500TS

### Features

**Max Brew:** 1.3l / 8 cups
**Carafe:** Thermal, stainless steel.
**Special features:** Wide showerhead design, preinfusion
**Brew time:** Around 6 minutes
**Material:** Stainless steel & plastic
**SCA Certified?:** Yes
**Warranty:** 2-year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### A Brand That’s Still Brewing

Bonavita has faced its fair share of recent controversy, from **legal disputes between its manufacturer and distributor** to rumors that the brand was on its way out. But like Mark Twain once said, **reports of its death have been greatly exaggerated**. According to the latest updates, those issues seem to be resolved, and Bonavita is back in action, alive and brewing.

#### Designed for Small Batch Excellence

While its larger sibling holds **SCA certification**, this smaller-capacity brewer shares many of the same high-quality design features. It **brews between 195-205°F**, which is exactly the temperature range you want for optimal coffee extraction. The **showerhead design ensures even saturation**, especially for smaller batches, and there’s even an **optional pre-infusion mode,** a feature often reserved for higher-end brewers.

#### Reliable, but Reputation Took a Hit

This machine has sold well and is generally well-loved on Amazon, but its **overall rating isn’t quite what you’d expect** for such a well-respected brewer. Much of the recent negativity seems tied to the **fallout from Bonavita’s distributor issues**.

To clarify:

If you purchased a Bonavita machine **before January 1, 2021**, your warranty is technically under the [**old distributor**](https://www.modernretail.co/retailers/the-rise-fall-and-potential-resurrection-of-a-coffee-brewing-legend/), who no longer offers support.

Bonavita says they’ll still offer customer support, but **no replacements or refunds** for those older units.
This situation has understandably ruffled feathers across Amazon reviews, [Reddit threads](https://www.reddit.com/r/Coffee/comments/tl8x34/a_warning_about_buying_from_bonavita/), and coffee forums.

#### Minor Flaws, Nothing Major

As for the product itself, most complaints are relatively minor.

The **thermal carafe can be tough to fully empty**, especially that last bit of coffee.

**Pouring without the lid** can be a little messy, which might be frustrating if you’re in a hurry.

#### Kev’s Take

If you’re looking for a **compact, no-nonsense drip brewer** that still ticks most of the specialty boxes, including proper brewing temp, a pre-infusion option, and a thermal carafe, this Bonavita is a solid option. Just **be sure your unit was purchased recently** to avoid warranty issues.

### Oxo 8-Cup Drip Coffee Maker

### Features

**Max Brew:** 64 ounces / 8 cups
**Carafe:** Thermal, dual-walled stainless steel.
**Special features:** Single serve option. Rainmaker shower head
**Brew time:** Approx 6-8 minutes for a full pot
**Material:** Stainless steel & plastic
**SCA Certified?:** Yes
**Warranty:** 2-year manufacturer’s warranty

### Kev’s Observations

#### Certified for Specialty Brewing

The OXO 8-Cup Coffee Maker is another SCA-certified brewer, which already gives it a leg up in terms of quality assurance. One thing I’ve noticed across these certified brewers is that they tend to **stick to the realistic 8-ounce ”standard cup” size** -no wild marketing claims like “12 cups” when they mean 4-ounce espresso shots.

#### Smart Features for Better Brewing

On paper, this is a well-equipped machine. Key features include:

The **RainmakerTM showerhead**, which evenly disperses hot water over the grounds

**BetterBrewTM Precision**, a system that optimizes brew temp, time, and volume

A **double-walled, vacuum-insulated thermal carafe**

A **single-serve brew mode**, which is handy for quick solo cups

All of this at a price point makes it one of the **best-value SCA-certified drip brewers** on the market.

#### Excellent Water Distribution

I have to say, the Rainmaker showerhead does look impressive. One of my only gripes with the Breville Precision Brewer was its showerhead’s size and distribution radius, it concentrated water too much toward the center.
With the OXO Rainmaker, though, you can expect a much **more even spread of water over the coffee bed**, which improves saturation and helps avoid uneven extraction.

#### Single-Cup Convenience, or Brew a Whole Pot

OXO gives you the option to brew a **single cup or a full 8-cup carafe**, which is great if you’re switching between solo sips and serving guests. That said,  customer reviews  **have mixed feelings**  about the carafe’s heat retention.

And I get it. I’ve seen this with other brewers, too. If you’re only brewing a small amount and the  **carafe is cold**, it’ll zap the heat from your coffee as it brews, and the final temperature will not be  there by the time the pot is done.

**Pre-warming the carafe** is highly recommended if you’re brewing less than a full pot. The same goes for the mug if you’re using single-serve mode. A stone-cold cup will soak up the first ounces of heat like a sponge.

#### Kev’s Take

The OXO 8-Cup is a **great compact brewer** for people who want **true drip coffee** without going overboard on features or price. It’s especially ideal if you want **SCA-certified quality in a simple package**, and it’s great for both everyday sippers and weekend entertainers.

## Drip Coffee Makers FAQs

### Q: Is there a difference between drip coffee makers?

**A:** Yes, for sure. The biggest difference is that there are [cheap, domestic drip coffee makers](https://coffeekev.com/best-coffee-maker-under-100/), and there are specialty drip coffee makers. The best way to ensure you’re getting the latter if this is what you want is to look for an SCA-approved drip coffee maker, as a number of the options above are. The biggest difference between “standard” drip coffee makers and specialty brewers is that brewers made for specialty coffee are designed to deliver a specific, precise brew temperature, and other key elements include the design of the showerhead to ensure evenly saturated grinds, specific flow rate, and bloom time & volume.

### Q: Is French press coffee better than drip?

**A:** Better is a subjective word, there’s really no such concept as “better“, just ”better for me“ - so where French Press vs drip coffee is concerned, which is better just comes down to which you prefer. French press coffee is characteristically a heavier brew in terms of mouthfeel, and usually a more intense brew in terms of flavor, although you can adjust this with your brewing technique.

### Q: How do you make drip coffee taste better?

**A:** The number one way to make your coffee taste better, regardless of the brew method, is to use better quality coffee. Look for coffee from a specialty small-batch coffee roaster, which has a roasted-on date of between 2-4 weeks from when you purchase it, and try various different coffees, as there are so many different tasting coffees available, from different origins, from different subspecies of Arabica.

Want to improve your coffee? Then watch this helpful guide

### Q: Is Espresso better than drip coffee?

**A:** If you prefer espresso to drip coffee, then yes. If you prefer drip coffee to espresso, then no. There’s no such thing as better or worse where taste is concerned, as we all have different taste buds. In fact, for me, it would depend on when you ask me. There are times when I’m in the mood for espresso or espresso-based drinks, and there are times when I’m in the mood for drip coffee.

### Q: Do all drip coffee makers taste the same?

**A:** I’ve never actually tasted a drip coffee maker, so I can’t help you with this one;-). If you’re referring to the taste of the drip coffee from various drip coffee makers, then no. Generally speaking, if you’re buying a low-priced ”normal“ drip coffee maker, then if you were to line up a number of them and try them all with the same coffee, I think you’d probably find that they’re all quite similar when it comes to taste.

If you were to brew a pot of the same coffee with a lower-cost ”normal“ drip coffee maker and also brew the same coffee with one of the premium, more home barista-grade specialty drip coffee brewers, then I would expect most people to be able to notice a difference in the taste. Not only this, but I’d expect the specialty coffee brewer to be more consistent from one pot to the next.

### A: Do you have milk with drip coffee?

**A:** WHAT???? Hehe, I’m just kidding. Sure, if you like milk, creamer, half & half, whatever you like with your drip coffee, why not? Heck, some people are even putting butter in their coffee these days! I say each to their own, personally, I drink my filter coffee (which is another label for drip coffee, by the way) black.

It does depend on what coffee you’re using, though. Many people add stuff to coffee, such as milk, creamer, and/or sugar or syrups, because it’s bitter and needs sweetening, and this is largely to do with the coffee itself.

If you’re using store-bought ”commodity“ coffee (coffee that is traded as a commodity like sugar and grain), it’s usually roasted dark to remove taste defects. It’s inherently bitter, which some people like, but some people don’t, hence the addition of stuff to sweeten it and mask the bitterness.

The first change you’ll probably notice if you start drinking specialty coffee is that you’re no longer as inclined to put anything in your coffee other than your face.

### Q: Is Nespresso drip coffee?

**A:** In a word, no. The original Nespresso machines make an espresso-style drink, short concentrated shots, which aren’t technically espresso as it’s brewed differently, but it’s closest to espresso. You can, of course, add hot water to Nespresso, and if you do that, then you’ll make something which is more akin to an Americano than drip coffee, which is similar but not quite the same. Generally speaking, drip coffee is lighter and cleaner than Americano and the Americano style coffee you’d get from adding hot water to a Nespresso.

There’s also the newer [Nespresso Vertuo machine](https://amzn.to/3gqgfHH), and this does have the option of pour-over style pods, but to me, these don’t look or taste anything like drip coffee. They have a big foamy crema, which is something I’d associate more with Americano, and they have the body and flavor of Americano more than drip coffee, just my humble opinion from the [Nespresso Vertuo pods](https://amzn.to/484cRrj) I’ve tried.
